title: Windows: document optional manual DXC setup for DX12
body:
## What and why

Closes #561. Windows users whose status bar shows Dx12 now have a short guide for optionally installing Microsoft's DXC themselves. Vulkan users need no setup. The guide links the official v1.9.2609 archive, gives its SHA-256, explains copying only the x64 `dxcompiler.dll` beside the executables, and shows how to confirm the loaded module. It also explains updater retention, manual updates and removal. DXC is downloaded by the user from Microsoft; FieldCraft does not redistribute it.

The Windows zip remains unchanged. This PR contains only `docs/windows-dxc.md` and links from the GPU performance documentation and Windows release notes. No packaging, runtime, updater, licence-policy, attribution or ROADMAP change remains in the feature history. The approximate 8-second/0.5-second pipeline times are explicitly attributed to the measured RTX 4090 example in #561, not asserted as new or universal results.

## Demonstration

A fresh 27.5-second native-window recording, `manual-windows-dxc.mp4`, shows the original heated-flow sample solving on RTX 4090 (Dx12), temperature frames and signed wall heat after **manual** DXC installation. Its captions state that the standard Windows zip is unchanged and that the verified Microsoft DLL was added by the user.

The demo uses a freshly extracted original seven-file Windows package containing no DXC. The downloaded archive matched `AD31B1FC8443175D204F77A611FDB3EF2EC42759BDC2F1167368DE24A4A7E7F1`; only `bin/x64/dxcompiler.dll` was manually copied into the installation folder. Module inspection confirmed that adjacent user-added DLL loaded, with the compiler override unset and DXC directories excluded from PATH. The app reports GPU execution on RTX 4090. Removing the DLL restored the original seven-file layout, and the app restarted successfully afterward.

The sample is a single-air-domain physical transient over a held 80 °C bracket: 5 mm cells, 5,824 total cells, 180 steps and 45 s. It is not a coupled two-fluid exchanger. The fresh video and `manual-temperature.png` / `manual-wall-heat.png` were pushed as verified ordinary Git blobs to the separate `artifact-queue` in commit `33a3913`, under this new tested head; the maintainer's `received` receipts are still pending. **Media remains pending until the maintainer supplies real GitHub attachment URLs.** Earlier bundled-package artifacts at head `3145551` were received but are immutable, superseded evidence and must not be attached as the demonstration of this revised PR.

## Validation

- Reviewed the three-file docs-only diff, archive/hash/module PowerShell instructions, local documentation target and release-note link. `git diff --check` passes. No code or package changes remain.
- Ran the unchanged production packaging script with the existing release-profile binaries; verified the zip has seven original files and no `dxcompiler.dll` or `dxil.dll` before manual setup.
- Followed manual installation on Windows 11 Pro build 26200, RTX 4090 driver 616.56; verified the user-added module path and hash, completed the native GPU/thermal sample, then removed the DLL and restarted. No new throughput or pipeline-time measurement is claimed.
- Verified updater retention with the existing Windows file-by-file mock updater fixture temporarily naming the user-added file `dxcompiler.dll`: one targeted test passed, source restored afterward. No updater code or test changes are included.
- Rebased onto the maintainer's current `upstream-develop` mirror before the exact-lease rewrite of this owned feature branch. No full local gates were rerun for documentation-only changes. Earlier CI results and bundled-package verification belong to the superseded head and are not asserted for this new head.

## Known limitations

Manual setup is optional and specific to DX12; Vulkan users need nothing. Timing varies with hardware, driver and workload. Older Windows 10/driver combinations were unavailable for this manual smoke test. The local app used the current unchanged developer binaries labelled 0.7.0; this is not a published release. Artifact receipt and GitHub attachment remain separate maintainer steps; no GitHub login or UI upload is required of agents.

comments.author: jyviko
comments.body:
@bluecmd, thinking about this more, I'd like to keep the Windows zip as it is and not ship the DLL ourselves. Vulkan is tried first and is already full speed for most Windows users (your own table in #561 shows it), so bundling 22 MB plus a build-time download and the extra licence notices costs everyone for the DX12-only case.

But your research is too good to lose. Could you turn this PR into **user instructions** instead? A short docs page, e.g. `docs/windows-dxc.md`, that tells someone on DX12 how to get the speed-up themselves:

1. **When it helps:** only when FieldCraft runs on DX12. The status bar shows the GPU and its backend; Vulkan users need nothing.
2. **Where to get it:** Microsoft's DirectXShaderCompiler release v1.9.2609, asset `dxc_2026_09_29.zip` (https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases/tag/v1.9.2609).
3. **Verify it:** `Get-FileHash dxc_2026_09_29.zip -Algorithm SHA256` must print `AD31B1FC8443175D204F77A611FDB3EF2EC42759BDC2F1167368DE24A4A7E7F1`.
4. **Install it:** copy only `bin\x64\dxcompiler.dll` next to `fieldcraft.exe` and `fieldcraft-cli.exe`. `dxil.dll` is not needed, and wgpu picks the DLL up by itself.
5. **Check it worked:** first GPU solve starts in about 0.5 s instead of ~8 s.
6. **Updates keep it:** the updater replaces only the files in the release zip. Delete the DLL to undo.
7. **Licence:** it's Microsoft's open-source compiler (NCSA/MIT), the user downloads it from Microsoft, and we don't redistribute it.

Then drop the packaging, ADR and ROADMAP changes. A link from the GPU section of the docs (and from the Windows release notes) would be great. Thanks again for the careful measurements, they're what made this an easy call! 🙏

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Thanks @bluecmd, this is a really careful piece of packaging work! 🙌 Pinning Microsoft's immutable release by SHA-256, reading exactly three bounded entries and leaving `dxil.dll` and the proprietary licence out is exactly how I'd want a third-party binary handled. And the throughput win from #561 is a big deal for Windows users.

I checked it independently: the URL is a real asset of the immutable v1.9.2609 release and the pinned hash matches it; the x64 `dxcompiler.dll` hashes to the value in your report and is a PE32+ DLL; wgpu-hal 30.0.1 (`dx12/instance.rs`) loads `dxcompiler.dll` by name and only falls back to FXC when it can't load it, and never loads `dxil.dll` (DXC's internal validator signs the shaders since 1.8.2502), so the benefit holds without it. The updater change is test-only; staging still takes the minisign-verified zip. `cargo test -p fieldcraft-update` 19/19, clippy and fmt clean on macOS.

A few asks inline.

inline_comments.author: jyviko
inline_comments.body: The notices may not be complete for what the DLL contains. `LICENSE-LLVM.txt` in the archive is just the NCSA text, but DXC's own `LICENSE.TXT` at v1.9.2609 also carries the Miniz notice (`lib/Miniz/*`), and the DLL links SPIRV-Tools (Apache-2.0; its pass help strings are in the binary). Could the package's licence file also carry DXC's `LICENSE.TXT`/`ThirdPartyNotices.txt` from the same tag and the SPIRV-Tools notice? Fetching them from the tagged source with pinned hashes would keep the same guarantees as the DLL.

inline_comments.author: jyviko
inline_comments.body: Same as on #704: could we leave ROADMAP.md out? I keep the roadmap myself.

inline_comments.author: jyviko
inline_comments.body: Small one: the doc records one run's test results ("17 passed and two existing Windows failures…"). That will go stale in the repo; could those numbers live in the PR description instead, with the doc keeping how to package and verify? Same for the matching lines in `docs/releasing.md`. Also, `test-dxc.ps1` isn't run by any workflow yet. Is it worth a step in the Windows packaging job so it doesn't rot?
